lines.text: When a publisher turns off its servers, the game you paid for goes with it.
Last Save is a game licence that outlives its publisher.
Players are demanding games that can't be switched off. Last Save lets a studio prove it, and earn on every resale.
Each licence is an NFT on NEAR. Forty percent of every sale is locked, by contract, for the day the studio leaves.
The server key sits in an enclave. Only this contract, running this exact program, can release it. Nobody can take it back. Not the studio. Not us.
Then the studio goes dark. No announcement. And its own word can't keep the game alive. Only players who are actually being served can.
Anyone can ask the enclave to check. Three probes fail. The contract declares the studio gone, and the enclave releases the server.
Every holder decides: take their share back, or keep the game alive. New players fund it too.
A fan runs one command. The released build checks out against the hash the studio committed to on day one.
Same players. Same progress. The host is paid per real player session, signed by the players themselves.
